name: verne-translation
description: Real TRANSLATION-collation case (BACKLOG B4): the opening paragraph of Jules Verne's 'Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas' (Part 1, Ch.1) in two competing English translations of the same French original — the 1872 Mercier Lewis 'standard' translation (abridging/altering) versus the faithful, unabridged F. P. Walter translation. This is NOT authorial revision but translation variation: it stress-tests the engine on heavy substantive substitution between two renderings of one source ('signalised'/'marked', 'remarkable incident'/'bizarre development', 'deeply interested'/'extremely disturbed'). Base = the older Mercier translation. See docs/development/CASE_STUDY.md.

source.work: Jules Verne, Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas, Part 1, Ch.1 ('The year 1866…'), first paragraph
source.mercier: Project Gutenberg eBook #164 (Lewis Page Mercier translation, 1872), verbatim
source.walter: Project Gutenberg eBook #2488 (F. P. Walter translation, complete/unabridged), verbatim
